history.dynasty: Reconstructed during the reign of King Kulachandra Singh of Manipur (1891 AD); one tourism source attributes the original shrine to the 15th century reign of King Khagemba (conflict - verify)
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. This is the principal temple of Sanamahism, the indigenous pre-Hindu Meitei religion, dedicated to Lainingthou Sanamahi, the supreme household deity of the Meitei people. It stands in the Sanakhwa Yaima Kollup near Kangla Palace (now in the 1st Manipur Rifles Ground), Imphal West district - the CSV town of Chandel is wrong; there is no documented Sanamahi Temple in Chandel district. The present octagonal brick structure with a pyramidal Gothic-style roof and flying steps on its southern side was reconstructed in 1891 AD under King Kulachandra Singh (one tourism source claims a 15th-century original under King Khagemba - verify). It is listed among Manipur's state protected monuments (S-MN-18) and is governed by the Lainingthou Sanamahi Temple Board. It is often confused with the newer Sanamahi Kiyong Temple atop Nongmaiching Hill in Imphal East (inaugurated 8 June 2019) - a separate site; do not conflate the two.

name: Sanamahi Temple
town_description: Imphal is the capital of Manipur, set in the central valley at about 786 m elevation, and the cultural heart of the Meitei people. The Kangla Fort precinct - the ancient seat of Manipuri kings - anchors its heritage landscape alongside the Shri Govindajee Temple, the Manipur State Museum and Ima Keithel (the women's market). It is served by Bir Tikendrajit International Airport and connects by road to Dimapur, Guwahati and Silchar.
tradition: Sanamahism (indigenous Meitei religion - pre-Hindu; NOT Hinduism)

travel.airport: Bir Tikendrajit International Airport, Imphal (approx. 7-8 km from the city centre; verify).
travel.railway: Manipur's only broad-gauge railhead is Jiribam railway station (approx. 210 km by road; verify); the nearest major railhead outside the state is Dimapur, Nagaland. Most visitors arrive by air or road.
travel.road: The temple is near Kangla in central Imphal, reachable by local taxi/auto from anywhere in the city; Imphal connects by NH-2/NH-37 to Dimapur, Kohima, Guwahati and Silchar.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (dry, pleasant season); Sajibu Nongma Panba (Meitei New Year, March-April) is the most significant festival period (verify dates).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published (verify - typically open morning and evening for daily puja; confirm locally). No entry fee expected; photography rules unknown.
